# Results — Study 628 (Buffett's Alpha)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Frazzini, Kabiller & Pedersen, **Buffett's Alpha**, FAJ 2018) — **Berkshire Hathaway's
four-decade CAPM alpha is real (t > 3), is largely explained by quality + low-beta exposure
financed with cheap insurance-float leverage, and has been fading** — audited on the public
tape: BRK-A monthly total returns 1980-2026 vs an honestly-spliced US-market total return,
excess-vs-excess, Newey-West HAC everywhere. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `96d18b13a5da`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Fund leg | **BRK-A** monthly total return, yfinance adjusted close (Berkshire has paid **no dividend since 1967**, so price = total return — no adjustment ambiguity) |
| Market leg | **spliced US-market total return, labeled per row**: 1980-04 → 1993-01 = ^GSPC month-end price return **+ Shiller monthly dividend yield** (154 months); 1993-02 → 2026-06 = **SPY** adjusted (total-return) monthly return (401 months) |
| Risk-free | 13-week T-bill (^IRX) discount yield at the **previous** month-end / 12 — the rate lockable at the start of each month (no look-ahead) |
| Window | 1980-04-30 → 2026-06-30 (**555 months, 46.2 years**) |
| Factor proxies | **QUAL** (MSCI USA Quality, live 2013-07) + **USMV** (MSCI USA Min-Vol, live 2011-10) monthly total returns — *investable ETF-era proxies*, **not** the academic QMJ/BAB long-short factors (labeled "factor-lite" everywhere) |
| Execution / costs | no timing rule — the only strategy is **buy-and-hold BRK** (one purchase, 46-year hold; a one-off ~5 bps spread is immaterial at this horizon). The one timing convention: the risk-free leg uses the *previous* month-end bill yield. Excess-vs-excess Sharpe races; all legs total-return |

> **Selection-on-success (named on the Signal axis).** Berkshire is on this bench *because
> it won*: it is the single most famous compounder alive, picked ex post. FKP themselves note
> BRK has the highest Sharpe of any US stock with 30+ years of history — a maximum over
> thousands of tries. The *t* = 3.47 below is the alpha of the *chosen winner*, not the alpha
> an investor could have expected ex ante by picking a conglomerate in 1980. The stamp grades
> the FKP claim (this specific fund's alpha is statistically real), and this caveat bounds it.

## The signal — the most famous alpha in the world, on the public tape

Full-sample CAPM, BRK excess on market excess, Newey-West lags = 5:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| $1 (1980-04) grows to | **BRK $2,880** vs market **$220** (18.80%/yr vs 12.37%/yr, total return) |
| excess return | BRK **+15.64%/yr** vs mkt +8.88%/yr |
| **CAPM alpha (full sample)** | **+9.46%/yr** · **HAC *t* = +3.47** (n = 555) |
| beta | **0.70** (t = 10.8) · R² = 0.24 · IR = 0.50 |
| Sharpe (excess-vs-excess) | BRK **0.72** vs mkt 0.59 (BRK vol 21.6%/yr) |
| FKP-era subsample (→ 2011-12) | alpha **+12.36%/yr** · HAC *t* = **+3.40** · beta 0.68 (n = 381) · Sharpe 0.72 vs 0.44 |

The FKP headline replicates on free public data: a four-decade alpha above **9%/yr** at
**HAC *t* = 3.47**, earned at a beta of only **0.70** — the low-beta signature FKP document.
On their own sample window (to 2011) our tape gives *t* = 3.40, matching their ">3" claim.
Clears the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar decisively. REAL — with the selection-on-success caveat above.

## The decay curve — where the alpha actually lives

Per-decade CAPM (2020s = partial decade, 78 months):

| decade | alpha (%/yr) | HAC *t* | beta | BRK excess | mkt excess |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1980s** | **+23.39** | **+3.55** | 0.82 | +31.25% | +9.58% |
| 1990s | +5.07 | +0.76 | 0.92 | +16.70% | +12.68% |
| 2000s | +6.01 | +1.28 | 0.47 | +4.88% | −2.41% |
| 2010s | +5.15 | +1.28 | 0.60 | +12.89% | +12.90% |
| 2020s (partial) | +2.06 | +0.34 | 0.71 | +11.40% | +13.13% |

Rolling **10-year** CAPM alpha (436 windows, ends 1990-03 → 2026-06): peak **+20.34%/yr**
(window ending 1990-03); latest **+1.83%/yr** (*t* = 0.46, beta 0.75); the **last window with
*t* ≥ 2 ends 2002-12** — no ten-year stretch in the last 23+ years certifies alpha on its own.
Only 25.0% of all windows clear *t* ≥ 2, all of them early.

**The fade is itself significant** (one regression, post-2010 dummy, HAC *t* on the
*difference* — a justified split: FKP's sample ends 2011):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| early alpha (1980-04 → 2010-12) | **+12.97%/yr** (*t* = +3.48) |
| **alpha change after 2010** | **−10.98 pp/yr** · **HAC *t* = −2.38** |
| beta change | +0.08 (*t* = +0.65, none) |

## Third axis — any alpha left in the last 15 years?

2011-07 → 2026-06 (180 months):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| CAPM alpha | **+2.66%/yr** · **HAC *t* = +0.89** |
| beta | 0.75 |
| Sharpe (excess-vs-excess) | BRK **0.74** vs mkt **0.90** |
| $1 grows to | BRK **$6.45** vs market **$7.37** |

No. The last-15-years alpha is statistically **zero** (*t* = 0.89), Berkshire's Sharpe is now
*below* the index's, and a dollar in BRK **lagged** a dollar in the S&P 500. The "fading"
half of the FKP claim is confirmed with room to spare — **BUSTED** on "any alpha left".

## Factor-lite attribution — the FKP mechanism, investable-proxy edition

On the common QUAL/USMV window (2013-08 → 2026-06, n = 155; *investable ETF proxies, not the
academic QMJ/BAB long-short factors — a factor-lite check, honestly labeled*):

| model | alpha (%/yr) | HAC *t* | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| CAPM alone | +1.54 | +0.46 | 0.41 |
| + QUAL + USMV | +1.43 | +0.44 | **0.51** |

Loadings: mkt **−0.17** (*t* = −0.37), QUAL **+0.30** (*t* = +0.68), **USMV +0.89**
(***t* = +3.77**). In the ETF era Berkshire prices like a **min-vol fund**: the USMV loading
is large and decisive, absorbs the market beta, and lifts R² from 0.41 to 0.51. Consistent
with FKP's low-beta/quality mechanism — though on this late window there is no alpha left for
the factors to "explain away" (it was already ~0 at CAPM). The era where factors could be
tested against a *live* alpha (1980s-90s) predates investable proxies; we say so rather than
pretend.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful

Seeded (market, manager) worlds with a **planted** CAPM alpha and AR(1) idiosyncratic noise,
**averaged over 20 seeds** (no single-seed baselines):

| planted alpha | mean recovered | mean HAC *t* | share of seeds \|t\| ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0%/yr** (null) | +0.27%/yr | **+0.11** | 10% |
| **+6%/yr** | +6.27%/yr | **+2.56** | 70% |

The null does not manufacture significance (mean *t* = 0.11); a planted 6%/yr alpha is
recovered without bias and lights up. *(Machinery proof only — never cited as market
evidence.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Buffett's alpha is the rare legend the tape certifies: **+9.46%/yr**
  full-sample CAPM alpha at **HAC *t* = 3.47** over 46.2 years (FKP-era subsample *t* = 3.40,
  matching the paper's *t* > 3), earned at beta 0.70. Carries an explicit
  **selection-on-success** caveat: the fund was picked *because* it won.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Buying Berkshire is trivially accessible (one BRK-B share,
  negligible costs, unlimited capacity) — but what you can buy **today** is beta 0.75 with a
  statistically-zero alpha: the alpha faded by **−10.98 pp/yr** after 2010 (HAC *t* = −2.38 on
  the difference), no 10-year window since 2002 clears *t* ≥ 2, and the last 15 years lagged
  the index. A real alpha you can no longer harvest — FRAGILE, not INVESTABLE.
- **"Any alpha left in the last 15 years?" — BUSTED.** +2.66%/yr at *t* = 0.89, Sharpe 0.74
  vs the market's 0.90, $6.45 vs $7.37 per dollar. The fading half of FKP's claim is now the
  loudest half.
